summary: The milestone completed 10 experiments in 13.2 minutes, including 3 compute-bound experiments. SOTA plain-text relation generation with exact prefix guidance was the longest compute-bound experiment at 12.32 minutes, but the supplied timing does not explain why.
bottlenecks_identified: SOTA plain-text relation generation with exact prefix guidance formed the critical path at 12.32 minutes, but the fallback timestamps do not isolate its slow stage.
Disk modification-time reconstruction lacks task phase boundaries, so it cannot explain the longest compute run.
The GPU report is a point-in-time snapshot, not a task-window trace, so it cannot establish utilization efficiency across compute-bound execution.
No launch record states loaded-model concurrency or runner selection, so DualGPURunner eligibility cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Emit per-experiment phase clocks for model load, inference, validation, and artifact writing.
Capture task-owned GPU utilization samples from each compute task's start through its finish.
Record loaded-model concurrency and runner choice in each compute launch receipt.
Select DualGPURunner only when a launch receipt confirms that 2 or more models load in parallel.
Replace disk modification-time reconstruction with a live milestone event log when the git-log path has no milestone commits.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add one task-owned receipt that joins phase timing, GPU samples, loaded-model concurrency, and runner choice.
Write live start and finish events so milestone timing does not depend on disk modification times.
Dispatch confirmed parallel multi-model work through DualGPURunner while leaving single-model work on one GPU.
meta_reflection: The locked task-level field does not flag GPU idle on compute-bound work. The available snapshot and fallback clock still leave the cause of the critical path and any parallel-model runner opportunity unverified, so the savings estimate remains 0 without a timed alternative.
